scope: Read-only planning assessment. No scheduler/helper/source edit, certificate read, case execution or scheduling change.
decision: Root retained the original sequential v1 scheduler; v2 concurrency would add resource and coordination work without requiring evidence changes midflight.
semantic_assessment: The two complete generation suites are independent if every existing case, verifier invocation, expected rejection, protected-output check, immutable identity and explicitly reused original control is preserved.
resource_findings: Existing helper file cap24GiB+64KiB is global;64KiB is not a proven per-original mutation-growth bound. Recompressed frames and rewritten terminal nouns may expand further.

The proposed stricter per-mutant min(original+32MiB,24GiB+64KiB) cap would require enforcement during writes; exceeding it would leave an unexecuted construction/resource failure, not a successful intended semantic rejection.

Disk reservations must include initial indexed result.dag up to16MiB per generation, in addition to four16MiB regenerated sidecars, positive extracted output, sentinels, indexes, logs and all existing retained bytes.

Two independent free-space checks do not provide atomic shared capacity reservation. Coordinator admission/lease and per-generation lifetime locks would be needed; the waiting v1 scheduler must not become a third writer.
Existing owned_bytes traversal can race with a concurrent unlink between is_file and stat; shared accounting or race-safe scanning would be required.
Two6GiB sampled process-group caps do not establish a hard12GiB host RSS ceiling. A coherent shared sample/stop path would be needed, and host-observation wording must remain explicit.
Shared resource failure must stop both owned process groups, preserve both partials and classify remaining cases unexecuted. Prior unexplained payloads must never be silently reclaimed.

Verifier24GiB wire allowance remains unchanged even if helper construction permits global slack. CPU/IO/hash contention can worsen existing deadlines; no automatic timeout increase/retry is justified.
limitations: Actual complete proof sizes and concurrent throughput were not measured by this assessment.
No v2 implementation or launch was authorized or performed; the original sequential scheduler remains selected.
